--- PART 1/4 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "We can use measurements to tune." and "Parent behavior probes: Against one_D_TFT: mutual_coop last5 1, own_coop after4 1, score 2.87 per round (287 total) which is near CC 3, recovered. Against four_D_TFT: not recovered, score 0.925 (bad), mutual 0. Parent fails to recover against 4 initial D then TFT?"
STRATEGY: Parent is a mostly TFT-with-forgiveness strategy that fails to recover against four_D_TFT. The trace simulates parent and other population strategies against controlled probes, and proposes a new adaptive strategy that cooperates initially, occasionally defects to exploit forgiving opponents, retaliates briefly, and defects on the last round.

--- PART 2/4 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Use these measurements when deciding what to retain or change to maximize cumulative tournament fitness."
STRATEGY: The parent is a forgiving, mostly-cooperating heuristic (slot 2) that defects only on high recent opponent defection, DD streaks, or random chances. The trace simulates it against TFT, always-D, slot 2, and other forgiving opponents, then designs an adaptive TFT-with-exploitation variant. Changes: add always-defect detection, last-round defection, early probing, retaliation-rate-based exploitation capped at 9 defections, and forgiveness when opponent defects after our own recent defection.

--- PART 3/4 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Let's test this against various opponents mentally." / "Against TFT (slot 9/4):" / "Against parent (slot0):"
STRATEGY: Parent is a forgiving Tit-for-Tat variant with early strict retaliation and later forgiveness; the trace simulates it against TFT, always-C, slot1, slot2, slot3, slot4, and parent, then revises the probe schedule to first defect at n=10 and then every 6 rounds with a cap of 9 defections, stopping scheduled defections if retaliation rate exceeds 0.3.

--- PART 4/4 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "So overall, this strategy seems very strong. It will score high against forgiving opponents (gain ~20 each) and slightly positive against TFT-like (+1 each)."
STRATEGY: Parent cooperates initially, probes at round 10, then defects every 6 rounds up to 9 times if retaliation is low, defects after 20 rounds of zero opponent defections, defects against heavy defectors, retaliates/forgives based on recent history, and defects on the final round. Simulated against always C, always D, TFT, forgiving slots, and parent. Changed by adding early heavy-defector detection, always-cooperator exploitation, retaliation-rate-gated scheduled defections, forgiveness after own recent defections, and a final-round defection.
